name: Byrnes Boulevard Waterfall Garden
description: A Byrnes Boulevard backyard at Country Club of South Carolina built around a stone waterfall and stream: brick and flagstone walks, planted beds in mulch and pine straw, and grading that carries water through the garden instead of across the lawn.
story: This Byrnes Boulevard property sits on a wooded Country Club of South Carolina lot that drops toward marsh and water at the back. The yard needed a way to handle that slope and still feel like a garden you walk through, not a leftover side yard. We built a multi-tier stone waterfall and stream as the spine of the space, with flagstone slabs crossing the flow and a brick paver patio and walks tying the house to the beds. Planting and groundcover follow the stone: mondo and iris at the water’s edge, shrubs and an ornamental tree in the pine-straw beds, and a river-rock edge where the drive meets the planting. Fresh pine straw and mulch finish the beds so the hardscape and the planting read as one job. The result is a backyard that uses the grade: water moves where it is meant to, walks stay dry, and the landscape holds together from the patio to the trees.
